payload.text: Explain your logic to find the two indices in an array that sum up to a target value.
expected_concepts: hash map enables O(1) complement lookup replacing inner loop
insert element into map AFTER checking complement — ensures you do not match element with itself
common_mistakes: inserts before checking complement — matches element with itself
stores value instead of index in hash map — cannot return correct indices
uses nested loops instead of hashing — O(n²) not O(n)
payload.reference_answer: The logic is to iterate through the array and for each element check whether the complement (target minus current value) has already been seen using a hash map.
possible_followups: O(n) time complexity with O(n) space trade-off
insert element into map AFTER checking complement to handle edge cases like target=2*element
handles duplicate elements correctly by checking before inserting
index stored in map not value (avoid overwriting)
explains why O(n²) brute force uses no extra space vs this approach
extends to two-sum on sorted array using two-pointer in O(1) space
handles case where same element cannot be used twice
